summary: Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who studied under Alexis Sanderson (~1990–1995) and earned his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1995–1997). He held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~2000–2007) and became a professor at Marburg around 2007.
Jürgen Neuß works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Harry Falk and completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2007.

Jürgen Renn works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at the Free University of Berlin (~1975–1982) and TU Berlin (~1983–1987), later holding posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (~1994–2023), FU Berlin (~1995), and Humboldt University (~2006).

K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who taught Dwijendra Nath Shukla. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and was a professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972 and 1987).
K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer was an Indologist who served as secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945) and as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras.

Indologist and linguist K. Kunjunni Raja earned PhDs at the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja and the University of London under John Brough. He was Reader In-Charge at Madras (~1954–1980) and Research Committee Chairman at Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (~1980–2005).

K. Meenakshi works in Indology and linguistics. She earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under Madhukar Anant Mehendale and held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who taught Hugo David, Steven Edward Lindquist, and Mattia Salvini. He held posts as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (attested 2008) and at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020).

K. T. S. Sarao is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees at the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge. He taught history at Kirori Mal College (1981) and became a professor at Delhi in 1995.

K. V. Ramesh was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986–1987) and as Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore (attested 2012).
K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian who served as Principal of Central Hindu College (~1935–1938) and as Principal at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1937–1939).

K. V. Sarma worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at the University of Kerala (~1937–1942). He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (~1943–1951), University of Madras (1951–1962), and Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre (~1991–2005).

K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Yongtong Tang, Sentian Wang, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi at Peking University and Visva-Bharati University. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Visva-Bharati and a visiting scholar at the Harvard-Yenching Institute.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo. He held a post as an assistant professor (助教授) at Rissho University (attested 2007).
Kaikyoku Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1900–1907). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1926–1933).

Kaiten Nukariya studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at Keio, Komazawa, and under Ryodo Nukariya. He lectured at Harvard (~1913–1914) and held posts at Komazawa University, including head teacher (1919) and first president (1925–1934), as well as Soto-shu University (~1921–1934).

Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who taught Koken Unno and Fujio Taniguchi. He served at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and later as a professor (attested 1999–2002).
Kalikinkar Datta was a historian and Indologist who taught Vishwanath Prasad Varma. He held a long post at Patna University (~1930–1965), where he also served as Vice-Chancellor (attested 1973).

Kalu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Palpung Monastery under teachers including Lama Norbu Dondrup, Khakyab Dorje, and Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo. He directed three-year retreats at Palpung Monastery (~1940–1955) and taught numerous students.
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is an Indologist, historian, and linguist who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as a professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).
